subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw add Markdown code-fence linting to workspace writes, and if so should it default to auto-fix, warn-only, or an explicit opt-in mode?
rationale: The request changes persisted workspace content and adds config/API surface, while prior PR review found parser edge cases that could corrupt real Markdown; automation cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Opt-In Or Warn-First Lint
options.body: Add a parser-backed warning or explicit opt-in fix mode first, keeping existing writes unchanged by default while maintainers evaluate false positives.

options.title: Default Auto-Fix
options.body: Make workspace Markdown writes rewrite code fences automatically, accepting a higher compatibility and content-mutation risk for stronger formatting guarantees.

options.title: No Core Write-Time Mutation
options.body: Keep core writes raw and rely on docs linting, prompts, or external tooling unless a narrower runtime bug proves a core hook is needed.

recommendation.title: Opt-In Or Warn-First Lint
recommendation.body: Add a parser-backed warning or explicit opt-in fix mode first, keeping existing writes unchanged by default while maintainers evaluate false positives.

likelyOwner.reason: The current workspace write and Markdown helper history points to this owner path, and the decision is about core write behavior rather than only the closed contributor branch.
